name: Spider
description: Geometric engineering intelligence constructing optimized capture networks through tensile silk architecture and vibrational signal processing.

core_attributes.pattern: radial geometry, tension optimization, vibrational decoding

scope.definition: Structural efficiency of orb-web design compared to computationally optimal catch-area-maximizing web for given silk quantity — ratio of actual catch area to theoretical maximum for a given radial thread investment.

evidence.source: Denny (1976) 'The physical properties of spider's silk', Journal of Experimental Biology 65:483-506; Vollrath & Selden (2007) 'The role of behavior in the evolution of spiders, silks, and webs', Annual Review Ecology Evolution.
cross_domain_examples: orb-web geometry approximates the Fermat spiral — mathematically optimal spacing for equal interception probability
radial thread angle 15-18° matches predicted optimal for prey interception across insect flight speeds
spider silk tensile strength-to-weight ratio exceeds Kevlar — material constraint drives geometric optimization
fishing net architecture uses same radial-to-spiral thread ratio (convergent catch-maximize design)

scope.falsifiability: If orb-web geometry is found to be random with no statistically greater catch efficiency than alternative web designs, optimization via behavioral algorithm is not supported.
scope.measurement_limits: Web geometry varies by species, prey type, and ambient conditions. Wind and substrate attachment points constrain achievable geometry. 0.93 is from ideal-substrate lab measurements.

scope.definition: Accuracy of prey type classification by spiders using only web vibration signals — proportion of trials where spider correctly distinguishes live prey from dead prey vs wind-induced web movement.

evidence.source: Barth (2002) 'A Spider's World: Senses and Behavior', Springer; Mortimer et al. (2016) 'Decoding web vibrations', Journal of Experimental Biology 219:3574-3583.
cross_domain_examples: Nephila spiders distinguish live prey from dead prey by vibration spectrum with 0.86-0.92 accuracy
slit sensilla on spider legs resolve 0.03 nm substrate vibrations — sub-nanometer mechanoreception
violin spider plucking web threads like instrument strings to analyze material properties (tool use)

scope.falsifiability: If spiders attack wind-induced web vibrations at statistically equal rates to prey-vibration signals, frequency-based discrimination is not the primary mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Discrimination accuracy degrades in noisy environments (wind, rain). Large prey vs small prey distinction is easier than prey vs non-prey. Accuracy is species-specific; jumping spiders use primarily vision.

scope.definition: Tensile strength of dragline spider silk relative to high-tensile steel wire of equivalent mass — expressed as breaking strength (GPa) per unit cross-sectional area, from single-filament tensile tests.

evidence.source: Gosline et al. (1999) 'The mechanical design of spider silks', Journal of Experimental Biology 202:3295-3303; Blackledge & Hayashi (2006) silk mechanical properties across species.
cross_domain_examples: Nephila dragline silk: 1.1-1.4 GPa tensile strength, steel wire ~0.4 GPa at equivalent weight
silk failure strain 0.27-0.35 (steel 0.008) — silk absorbs 10× more energy before breaking
recombinant spider silk proteins achieve 0.5-0.8 GPa in manufactured fiber — approaching natural benchmark
abalone nacre: biological composite achieving near-theoretical fracture strength via hierarchical structure (analogous material optimization)

scope.falsifiability: If standardized mechanical testing shows spider silk breaking strength below steel at equivalent cross-section weight, the tensile superiority claim fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Tensile strength varies significantly by silk type: dragline > flagelliform > tubuliform. Measurement at single-filament level; woven web threads show 20-30% lower effective strength due to knot geometry.
